name: IGF-1 LR3

lead: IGF-1 LR3 is a lab-modified version of insulin-like growth factor 1, sold to bodybuilders as an injectable for muscle growth and healing, sometimes stacked with insulin or steroids. The payoff people want is larger muscle, including targeted size where it is injected.

It activates the IGF-1 receptor and downstream PI3K/Akt/mTOR signalling. An extra amino acid chain and an arginine swap reduce binding to IGF binding proteins, so it is roughly three times as potent as native IGF-1 and lasts about 20 to 30 hours instead of 12 to 15. Evidence comes from cell and animal studies; no published human trial has tested it for muscle growth in healthy people.

paras: Sold as a research chemical for injection, used in bodybuilding circles alongside other agents. Forum discussion covers local-site growth and bloat, though these claims are not backed by trials.
Not approved for humans and banned in sport. Main concerns are low blood sugar, fluid retention, joint pain and organ growth, plus theoretical cancer promotion. Products are unregulated.

angle.text: IGF-1 LR3 is an injectable growth-factor analogue sold to bodybuilders for muscle growth and repair, sometimes stacked with insulin or steroids, aiming at larger muscle and local size. Cell and animal studies show IGF-1 signalling drives growth. Claims about local injection growth and bloat come from forums and vendors.

lead: IGF-1 LR3 (long arginine 3 insulin-like growth factor 1, also written LR3-IGF-1 or Long R3 IGF-1) is a synthetic, lengthened analogue of human insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1). It differs from the natural hormone by an arginine in place of glutamic acid at position 3 and an extra 13 amino acids at the N-terminus, giving a protein of 83 amino acids compared with 70 for native IGF-1.[1][2]

These changes leave it able to activate the IGF-1 receptor while sharply reducing its binding to the IGF-binding proteins that normally restrain IGF-1 in the blood. As a result, Wikipedia reports it is roughly three times as potent as IGF-1 and has a half-life of about 20 to 30 hours, compared with about 12 to 15 hours for IGF-1.[1] In bodybuilding forums it is discussed as an injectable compound used alongside other agents.[3][4]

IGF-1 LR3 is not an approved drug, and no published human trial has tested it for muscle growth, appearance or other benefit in healthy people. Evidence for its effects comes from cell and animal studies of IGF-1 signalling, and it falls under anti-doping rules covering growth factors.[5]
infobox: 83 amino acids: Arg3 substitution plus 13-residue N-terminal extension[1]
About 3 times IGF-1 potency; half-life about 20 to 30 hours (vs 12 to 15 for IGF-1)[1]
No approved human use identified in the sources reviewed[1][2]
Prohibited (WADA S2: peptide hormones, growth factors)[5]

paras: Long R3 IGF-I was designed and characterised in the mid-1990s as an IGF-I variant with enhanced potency in cell systems, and a research literature on its detection in doping control and in biological samples has since developed.[6][7] The arginine-for-glutamate swap at position 3 and the N-terminal extension reduce affinity for IGF-binding proteins and improve metabolic stability, so more of the peptide remains free to bind the receptor.[1][2] The same strategy appears in other IGF-1 analogues such as des(1-3)-IGF-1 and R3-IGF-1, which detection methods are designed to distinguish.[7]

IGF-1 LR3 binds and activates the IGF-1 receptor, with signalling through the PI3K/Akt pathway and downstream mTOR. In the research literature on native IGF-1, activation of this pathway inhibits FoxO transcription factors and expression of atrophy-related ubiquitin ligases such as atrogin-1 in muscle cells, which is the mechanistic basis often cited for IGF-1 as a muscle-growth factor.[8][9][10] Reviews of IGF-I as a skeletal-muscle therapeutic discuss the potential of IGF-1 and its optimisation, and metabolic studies of muscle hypertrophy have found IGF-1 treatment alters glucose-pathway metabolites in cultured muscle cells.[11][12]

Because IGF-1 signalling is also involved in cell proliferation, reviews of IGF-1 biology link the pathway to cancer cell glucose metabolism and to sebaceous gland growth and acne, and a 2023 study reported that an androgen receptor/miR-221/IGF-1 pathway mediates the pathogenesis of androgenetic alopecia. These studies concern native IGF-1 and not LR3 specifically.[13][14][15][16]

Related research on the broader IGF-1 category, not on LR3 itself: the broader IGF-1 literature includes studies of IGF-1 signalling in muscle cells and mice, and observational and mechanistic work linking IGF-1 to acne, cancer and metabolism.[8][9][14][15] A sports-endocrinology review addresses the prevalence of IGF-1 use among athletes and gym clients, its forms of use, ergogenic effects and side effects, as well as anti-doping detection methods, but it covers IGF-1 as a class and not specific clinical trials of LR3.[5]

Safety in humans has not been established. Concerns raised include effects on glucose handling, because IGF-1 shares signalling with insulin, and theoretical promotion of tumour growth, because IGF-1 signalling drives proliferation and glucose metabolism in cancer cells.[9][15] Forum users also ask about localised swelling or 'bloat'.[17] A sports-endocrinology review analyses side effects of IGF-1 use among doping substances but covers IGF-1 as a class.[5]

Peptide hormones, growth factors and related mimetics, including IGF-1 and its analogues, are prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency in and out of competition, and analytical papers describe mass-spectrometry methods for detecting LongR3-IGF-I, des(1-3)-IGF-I and R3-IGF-I.[5][7]

subs.h: Use in physique and looksmaxxing communities
paras: On T Nation, IGF-1 LR3 is discussed in the context of advanced bodybuilding regimens, often with insulin, growth hormone, GHRP-6 or anabolic steroids, and questions recur about route of injection, anti-doping detection and whether it causes localised muscle swelling.[18][17][3][4] One forum post links an article describing IGF-1 as promoting healing and muscle growth while acknowledging cancer concerns.[19] Posters also discuss pairing it with insulin and with steroids such as trenbolone.[20]
